title: Three Ways To Practice With Emptiness
speaker: Heigaku Talus Latona
summary: Heigaku Talus Latona takes up three ways to practice with emptiness, beginning with the Anattalakkhana Sutta, in which the Buddha tells the group of five monks that each of the five skandhas is non-self. Faith comes next, through Tenshin Reb Anderson's instruction to rise at the wake-up bell and the meeting of the nun Chi-Kwang with a 102-year-old Korean nun in The Hidden Lamp. The third way, holding boundlessness as an attitude, is illustrated by a coworker furious over a delayed request for lightbulbs, where everyone involved is acting out of care for patients. Heigaku ends by describing mourning for the dead as joyous and asking whether this practice is better called an attitude or a perspective.
